verdict.rationale: Granola Chat accepts natural-language requests: users can query one meeting, a folder, or all meetings, and can ask it to draft and send follow-up emails, send Slack messages, and create Google Calendar events, with a review step before anything is sent. Recipes save these prompts for one-click reuse. The evidence covers querying notes and post-meeting actions in other apps, not control of Granola itself (organizing folders, starting recordings, changing settings) through natural language. Missing for 10: natural-language control of core in-app operations such as folders, recording and settings; independent or hands-on corroboration of Chat-driven actions.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Granola Chat lets you ask questions about your meetings and get instant insights from your notes or transcripts.
You can use Chat from your home screen to query all of your meetings, on a single meeting, or in any other set of meetings such as a folder
Use Granola Chat to draft follow-up emails, send Slack messages, and schedule Google Calendar events — with a review step before anything is sent or created.
Ask Chat to: draft and send a follow-up email * draft and send a Slack message * find a time and create a Google Calendar event
you can save your favorite prompts as recipes and run them with a single click.
